text: hey in the studio how is it that when you click a face, and solidify, that the solid, is still all one face?
resolution: Answered why a solidified face still selects as one face: deliberate group inheritance in the native solidify. framework/gpu/3d.zig meshSolidifySelection (line 3724) gives every NEW triangle — the inner skin (line 3809) and rim-wall quads (lines 3828-3829) — the SAME authored face-group as the outer face it came from ('inner skin picks/paints with its outer face... so part ranges are untouched'). Studio face-picking selects by authored group (mesh_edit.zig setFaceGroup line 1625), so the whole slab (outer+inner+walls) is one clickable/paintable face by design. No code changed; flagged the tradeoff (rim/inner can never be individually selected, group also drives edge-boundary logic) and what a change would take (fresh group ids per new face + part-range growth).
